Let me think this through like I do every year before the season.

I farm 200 mu — that's a lot of land for just me and my wife. I can't manage it all by myself, so I hire help for busy times like wheat harvest and maize planting. Our main system here in Quzhou is wheat-maize double cropping, same as every family around here. I'll put 180 mu in wheat-maize rotation. The other 20 mu I split: 10 mu for cabbage because the price is decent when the market is right, and 10 mu for millet on the sandy patch where wheat doesn't do well.

For wheat, last year I got about 500 kg per mu. I use improved variety seeds from the county seed station — Jimai type, everyone around here uses these. I apply two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, that's about 50 kg, and then urea at jointing stage, maybe 20 kg. So roughly 25 kg nitrogen per mu total. Phosphorus and potassium from the compound, around 8 kg each. I irrigate 3 times with my well — before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. I spray herbicide once and pesticide for aphids once, sometimes twice if the worms are bad.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest — no time to waste. I use Zhengdan hybrid, good yield. I put urea about 25 kg per mu split in two times, plus a bit of compound at planting. Rain usually helps but I irrigate once if dry in July. One spray for borer is enough most years. I don't plough — I just do rotary tillage because ploughing costs too much and the land is fine.

For cabbage, it needs more fertilizer and water. I use hybrid seed. More nitrogen, maybe 30 kg per mu, because cabbage eats a lot. Needs 5-6 irrigations and more sprays for worms — cabbage worms are terrible.

For millet, I don't spend much. It's tough, grows on poor land. Traditional seed I save myself. Little fertilizer, no irrigation, one spray maybe.

I prefer to put a little extra fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. Fertilizer is expensive but losing yield is worse.
